answer.patch:
diff --git a/src/click/core.py b/src/click/core.py
--- a/src/click/core.py
+++ b/src/click/core.py
@@ -810,5 +810,16 @@ class Command:
             # Apply help_option decorator and pop resulting option
             help_option(*help_option_names)(self)
-            self._help_option = self.params.pop()  # type: ignore[assignment]
+            help_option_obj = self.params.pop()
+            param_names = {param.name for param in self.params}
+
+            if help_option_obj.name in param_names:
+                name = help_option_obj.name
+
+                while name in param_names:
+                    name = f"_{name}"
+
+                help_option_obj.name = name
+
+            self._help_option = t.cast("Option", help_option_obj)
 
         return self._help_option
answer.notes: Reproduced with a command declaring an argument named help. Without the patch, invoking it with a value lets the automatic --help option consume the same parser destination, triggering the help callback and exiting. The fix gives the generated help option a collision-free parameter name when a user parameter already uses its derived name. Local checks: reproduction emits the argument value; --help still prints usage/help for the same command; ordinary command help is unchanged; a parameter named _help also avoids collision via the while loop.
